title: Recruitment — the funnel from first contact to the flip
objective: The club can run a recruitment season out of the application instead of out of one person's head and a WhatsApp group. An operator holding the core four authority can capture a recruit at any of the four doors without creating a duplicate; read every recruit on one board as one line with the signals the platform can honestly observe; keep notes and see who wrote them; ask a recruit for their details and their football background and record what they choose to answer; schedule a recruitment event, invite recruits and players together, and take attendance on the day; and — when leadership decides somebody is in — flip them onto the roster with one audited action that creates the season membership and opens onboarding. Mission 5 gives recruitment the person; Mission 7 takes the member; everything between first contact and the flip is this mission's, including the administration of it.
why_now: Recruitment is the only Release One subject with no home in the application at all: the walk-up door is the sole part that exists on main, and it mints a prospect as a side effect of attendance with nowhere to read the result. Freshers' Fair is the club's single largest intake moment of the year and it is run on paper and memory. Two defects in the shipped event machinery also make the gap actively harmful rather than merely absent: scheduleEventLadder chases a recruit with the player escalation, and countByCapacity omits recruits from the approval summary, so an operator approves a recruitment event without being told how many recruits it reaches.
non_goals: Everything after the flip — the onboarding checklist, activation, the chase, the collection request, CSV import and carry-forward, and the LAN-85 intake-at-scale composition. Mission 7's.
The person record and the People and Roster surfaces themselves. Mission 5's; this mission layers onto them and invents none of them.
Consent policy, wording, lawful basis and retention rules. Mission 8's — recruitment records the evidence, Mission 8 says what it must mean.
Erasure. Removing a person is Mission 8's and never recruitment's; leaving the board is a status change and nothing more (owner decision 2026-08-25).
Transport, scheduler and template machinery. Mission 4's, used verbatim.
The Monday report and the export machinery. Mission 10's.
Club roles and the capability catalogue. Mission 1's — no new capability is minted for recruitment.
Any WhatsApp composer, free-text send, or two-way chat. src/lib/delivery/config.ts permits nothing but approved templates in production.
Real recruit data and real sends. LAN-86 and LAN-101 remain gates outside this mission.
Mission Lead decomposition, work packages or sequencing. Not in this packet, and no execution before Brian merges it.

requirements.text: Four capture doors exist and each captures first name, last name and mobile with email optional: QR/link self-entry on the club's own domain, walk-up capture from any event's attendance sheet, operator manual add, and the WhatsApp community route. Every door runs duplicate resolution before create, and none of them ever runs it at the flip.

Walk-up capture stays available on every event type to anyone taking attendance, including a coach holding one of the ten fixed coaching roles. Collecting walk-ups is part of attendance everywhere, not a recruitment-only affordance, so nothing about its placement changes. Every walk-up is a recruit.

Recruitment has its own board at /operate/recruitment, reached from a Recruitment destination in the top group of the left navigation under Roster. It is built like the Roster board: person details first, then recruitment details, event columns appended at the right, one line per recruit, findable and filterable, with actions from the row. It renders as a table above md and as cards below it, from one dataset.

One recruit's record at /operate/recruitment/[prospectId] carries the whole recruit on one page, built on the shipped player record's banded cards: person, recruitment, the questionnaires, recruitment events, notes with their authors and dates, and status history. Person facts route out to Mission 5's record and are never corrected here.

There is exactly one recruitment status on the prospect record, with seven values: identified, engaged, committed, joined, declined, disengaged and void. It is not tiered and not split into on-board and off-board sets; whether a recruit appears on the board is a display rule read off this one field. Recruitment never invents a membership status.

Recruitment is operated by the core four roles only — President, Vice President, Secretary and General Manager. The board, the record, the notes, the doors and the flip are theirs. No new capability is minted. The one carve-out is the coach at the touchline, who records a walk-up as attendance and never sees the board. Prospect records, signals and notes are never player-visible.

A recruit is never treated harshly: no player-grade escalation rung, no collection cadence, and no message telling a recruit they are required to be somewhere at a particular time. Polite reminders, nudges and operator follow-ups are expected, and making one easy and good to send is this mission's work.

The player chase stops reaching recruits, and recruitment's own ladder is built beside it: an invitation and at most one polite follow-up, then silence. The two ladders are configured on the messaging schedule's Recruitment event row as two named groups — Regular players keeping the shipped six-field chase that ends with the President, and Recruits carrying a first invitation and one follow-up with no escalation field at all.

Two verified defects at the baseline are fixed: scheduleEventLadder inserts a reminder job for every invitation filtered only by event_id, so a recruit invited today receives the player escalation; and countByCapacity omits recruits from the approval summary, so an operator approves a recruitment event without being told how many recruits it reaches.

A recruitment cycle fires after capture and is administered on the messaging schedule beside the seven event types: a welcome on capture for the walk-up and operator-add doors only, a personal-details ask, its single reminder, a recruitment-questionnaire ask, and its single reminder. There is never a second reminder for any step, and nothing at all is sent to a recruit who declined.

Every message a recruit receives is a Meta-approved WhatsApp template. No composer, no free text and no two-way chat exists anywhere in this mission, because src/lib/delivery/config.ts permits nothing else in production: template is the only production shape.

Asking a recruit about themselves and asking about their football background are two separate questionnaires with two separate sends, both on the shared signed-link form substrate at /a/[token]. Questions carry the answer control they deserve: yes-or-no for whether they have played or watched American football before, a chooser where the answers are a fixed set, and fill-in text only where the answer is genuinely open.

A recruit sees only an event's public details — never attendance, never who else was invited or answered, never roster or member data. A recruit invited to an event answers in WhatsApp and lands on the shipped /rsvp/[token] saved page, yes or no. There is no event page for a recruit.

A recruit is never asked why they are not coming. The rsvp_responses_no_requires_a_reason constraint is not weakened: for a recruit the system supplies the reason itself and never puts the question to them.

A recruitment event's audience builder offers all active players and all active recruits as group buttons, so an operator can invite both and then pick individuals out of the list. The recruits group is offered on a Recruitment event and on no other type.

Before approving a recruitment event, an operator can see on the event's own messaging plan exactly what approval will send, grouped by audience: the players' rungs ending with the President, and the recruits' rungs ending after one follow-up with no escalation row present.

On a recruitment event's attendance sheet, recruits are their own group at the top and everyone else is below, using the sheet's own shipped group markup. Attendance reads back onto the recruit's row and record. RSVP and attendance are always distinct: attending is intent, present is observed attendance.

The duplicate check runs as a step inside whichever door is open, on that door's own surface, and never as a page an operator visits. It shows each candidate saying who it is — membership status, season, or recruit rung — and the operator either links to the person already there or creates a new one, on the spot. Nothing is parked and there is no review queue. A duplicate that still gets through is resolved by the people record's own merge at /operate/people/[personId]/merge, which already ships and belongs to Mission 5. The walk-up door at the touchline deliberately runs no check at all.
requirements.original_text: A capture the system could not safely resolve is parked rather than silently created, merged or messaged, and waits in an operator review queue at /operate/recruitment/review until one of the core four decides it is the existing person or a new one.

requirements.text: The flip to joined is the four roles only and is one audited action. It interrupts with a confirmation over the surface where the decision is made, naming what it will create — the season membership, the roster place, onboarding — and what it will not do: make the person active. Cancelling writes nothing. One membership per person per season is the only guard at the flip; there is no duplicate check there.

Taking a recruit off the board is a status change and nothing more: no archive and no delete. The row, the record, every signal and every note stay, and the ladder stops reaching them. disengaged is explicitly recoverable, and coming back creates no new person and no second recruit row.

One sign-up QR code exists per season, minted once, on its own page reached by a QR CODE button on the recruit board. It points at the club's own page on the club's own domain — a recruit signing in to the club's application, not into a form elsewhere.
Missing information never blocks a capture and never blocks the flip, and nothing about a recruit is scored, ranked or advanced automatically by a computed value.

Every table this mission adds enables RLS in its creating migration and revokes all privileges from anon, authenticated and service_role before granting only the narrow server need, as recruitment_prospects already does. The service layer is the primary authorization boundary; RLS is the backstop.

decisions.text: No split. The four doors, the board, the record, the questionnaires, the events, the administration and the exits are one commissioned outcome and are not independently acceptable.
decisions.source: Commissioned outcome and the rare-splitting rule

decisions.text: The approved boundary is the recruitment subject, not the portfolio row's bullet list — Brian's direction of 2026-08-28 read under portfolio rule 1. The 43-item inventory in 00-boundary.md governs.

Recruitment is the core four roles only. This narrows Task 09 D9, which made prospect records visible to the operator group at large. Bringing coaches or anyone else in is a later decision, not a Release One one.

The never-chased system property becomes never-harsh. The message inventory is no longer capped at one touch per event; polite reminders and operator follow-ups are expected, and the prohibition is on player-grade harshness.
Recruitment is a top-level destination under Roster at /operate/recruitment, not an Administration entry. Brian, 2026-08-31, after the first build put it in Administration.

Events are the signals. There is no separate engagement-signal concept and nothing is conflated: the recruit's record shows the event, the RSVP and the attendance as distinct columns, in the club's own attendance vocabulary.
Free text about a recruit is notes, and notes live on the recruitment record with their author and date rather than on the person.
Committed on is the moment the recruit becomes joined, not an earlier soft commitment.
Personal details and football background are two questionnaires and two sends, not one form. Brian, 2026-08-31: they are two separate flows and both belong to W4.
W3 is removed rather than renumbered. Its five decisions moved to W10 and W2, the number is kept as an empty slot and never reused, and W4 through W14 hold the numbers they were frozen with.
W9 is folded rather than renumbered. Three of its four screens had already been built into W2 and the fourth — the refusal — became W2-04. Its three decisions moved to W10 and W2.
W15, the recruit messaging flow, was added on 2026-08-31 and removed the same day. Its content is the last section of W11's specification and the number is dead like W3 and W9.

The sign-up QR is reached by a button on the recruit board and has its own page. It is not on the messaging schedule: Brian, 2026-08-31, that doesn't make any damn sense for the QR code to go on the messaging page.
One QR per season, minted once, rather than one per event.
No page listing WhatsApp templates is built. A Meta-approved template is created in Meta's own tooling, so a page listing them would manage nothing; the approval gate survives as an owner action.
A declining recruit is never asked for a reason. The database constraint stands and the system supplies the reason itself.

The two ladders are split in the body of the messaging schedule's Recruitment event row rather than as a second row, so that one row per event type and one save per row — both laws of that page — survive.

The flip to joined is the only interruption in the exits. Declining, disengaging and coming back are one status control each, with no confirmation screen and no callout. Brian, 2026-08-31: we don't need callouts for this thing, the only time we need it is for Join.

void is a marker that the record is wrong rather than a statement about the person, and is proposed as a separate marker rather than a seventh ladder rung. Open for the Mission Lead to implement as recorded in W13.

The vocabulary is walk-up. WALK_UP_HEADLINE, WALK_UP_SUBMIT and WALK_UP_CHIP in the attendance presentation are corrected by this mission, and the recorded confirmation is a short Walk-up added rather than a paragraph.

The three operator-facing doors hold three deliberate duplicate postures: the walk-up door checks nothing at the touchline, the manual add runs the full check, and the self-entry door asks one question. This is intended and is not an inconsistency to normalise.
No operator composer is built at any point in this mission, in any workflow, because templates are the only production shape.

owner_amendments.title: The sign-up form is the single consent gate; consent is season-scoped
owner_amendments.text: The sign-up form is the mission's single consent gate and is the same surface as Questionnaire A. Every door leads to it: the QR points straight at it, and the walk-up and operator-add doors send one template carrying a signed prefilled link to it. No WhatsApp message ever asks permission to send WhatsApp messages. Consent is season-scoped, keyed (person_id, season_id), and gates every send in that season; granted, it carries from recruit through onboarding to player with no second ask, and each new season is re-approved. First and last name are the only required fields. recruit_details_ask is withdrawn because the welcome carries the form and is itself the ask. An opt-out honoured across channels is required by Meta and is built in this mission, so Channel Presence arrives early as a deliberate data-model amendment.

I'm not making new rules here... that's a normal merge record that is handled on the people record." This confirms the deletion already recorded in W8 on 2026-08-31.
